target_customer: Engineering teams that wanted a Heroku-style deploy workflow inside their own cloud account
problem: Heroku-style platforms were convenient but expensive and locked teams into a shared host, while running your own infrastructure was complex.
business_model: Flat platform fee on open source PaaS, customers pay their cloud provider directly
product_category: Platform as a service in the customer's own cloud

founders.name: David Dollar
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

founders.name: Noah Zoschke
founders.background_notes: YC page lists early Heroku, CTO at Housecat, Segment, and VP Engineering at GRAX; the later roles postdate the founding.

founders.name: Matt Manning
founders.background_notes: No background on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a Heroku-like workflow on AWS with containers took real infrastructure engineering, but used existing building blocks.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code and a crowded PaaS field meant easy copying. Deployed workloads gave some lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AWS and Kubernetes tooling absorbed much of the wedge over time. Convox was bought by Curious in April 2024 after about a decade.

market_need_then: Teams in 2015 loved Heroku's workflow but disliked its cost and lock-in, and containers on AWS were becoming practical.

branding.community_and_virality: Open source Rack project is mirrored on GitHub and SourceForge.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is confused with Convoy and Convex in searches; no brand press found.

outcome_analysis: Convox sold an open source Heroku-style PaaS that ran in the customer's own cloud, stayed small and survived roughly nine years until Curious acquired it in April 2024. It is listed as acquired but still operates with thousands of claimed customers. Its modest funding and slow path suggest a capital-efficient niche business rather than a venture-scale breakout.
notes: GeekWire fetch returned 403, so acquisition rests on search snippets plus CB Insights. CB Insights lists about 1.42M raised over four rounds (seed August 2015, debt November 2015, acquisition financing April 2024) with Garage Capital, Heavybit and YC as investors, unverified from a single aggregator so no rounds recorded. Competition search returned only undated StackShare comparisons, so the list is empty; Deis and Flynn were Heroku-style PaaS projects of the period but no dated source was found. Completeness pass: seed (Aug 2015) and debt (Nov 2015) rounds recorded from CB Insights with no amounts; total 1.42M over four rounds is per CB Insights, so the amounts are a known gap. The fourth entry (April 2024 acquisition financing) relates to the Curious acquisition and is not recorded as a funding round. Rounds rest on a single database.
